newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to sign Vatican pact on June 20 - official.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to sign Vatican pact on June 20 - official.

text.p: Prime Minister Gyula Horn will this month sign an agreement with the Vatican on the financing of Hungary's Roman Catholic Church despite recent controversy within the coalition government over the move, Hungarian officials said on Thursday.

"It cannot happen that such a pre-announced signing be postponed," Andras Toth, Prime Minister Gyula Horn's cabinet chief, told a news conference following the weekly government meeting. The signing will take place on June 20, he said.

Horns' coalition partners, the Free Democrats, have criticised the agreement on the grounds that singling out one religion for support might be unconstitutional and could have a negative effect on the funding of other independent schools.

Toth, who was the chief negotiator of the pact with the Holy See, said the agreement did not amount to discrimination between Hungary's churches but added that it had to be done because only the Vatican is entitled to sign financial agreements concerning Roman Catholic churches.
Hungarian press reports said the Free Democrats have convened the dispute settlement body, the Coalition Consultative Counci, to discuss the issue on Monday.
Socialist deputy Culture Minister Zoltan Szabo said the law was not biased on school funding and denied he had a different position on the issue from Free Democrat Culture Minister Balint Magyar.
Government spokesman Elemer Kiss said in an answer to a question that both officials were representing the government's point of view regarding church financing.
